newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- APPLE DAILY - About 2,000 people hit the streets in Hong Kong to urge Beijing to release jailed dissident Wang Dan.
-- MING PAO DAILY - China hopes to station about 300 advance People's Liberation Army personnel in Hong Kong early next year.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - Several Chinese officials including the Director of the Xinhua News Agency Hong Kong branch, Zhou Nan, deputy-governor of the People's Bank of China, Chen Yuan, and the Director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Lu Ping, denied the existence of a "central reserve" to bail out Hong Kong's stock market if necessary after the handover.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL - Hong Kong and Shanghai Hotels Ltd said that it would raise its room rents by six to 10 per cent next year.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Former Immigration Director Laurence Leung said that all the allegations against him that appeared in the press recently were unfounded.
- Cable and Wireless's ambitions to build a significant presence in the United States received a blow after British Telecom agreed a 12.5 billion stg merger with MCI Communications.
-- China's banks face millions of dollars in loan write-offs after almost 1,000 corporate creditors were forced to close under a federal anti-pollution campaign.
